readings: Match each player_college record to its player by player_id, dropping records with no matching player. Group by birth_country and treat a NULL birth_country as its own group, so it counts as a country. Count the records per group and compute each group's share of the total count. The overall average is the mean record count across all groups, including the NULL group. Keep only the groups whose count is strictly above that average. In one row, give the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average of (count minus overall average). Don't round anything.

Match each player_college record to its player by player_id, dropping records with no matching player. Also drop matched records whose birth_country is NULL, so only real countries remain. Count the records per birth_country and compute each country's share of the total count of the remaining records. The overall average is the mean record count across these non-NULL countries. Keep only the countries whose count is strictly above that average. In one row, give the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average of (count minus overall average). Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT p.birth_country AS bc, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM player_college pc
  JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id
  GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
t AS (
  SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g
)
SELECT SUM(g.cnt) AS sum_counts,
       AVG(g.cnt * 1.0 / t.total) AS avg_share,
       AVG(g.cnt - t.avg_cnt) AS avg_diff
FROM g, t
WHERE g.cnt > t.avg_cnt;
WITH c AS (
  SELECT p.birth_country AS country, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM player_college pc
  JOIN player p ON pc.player_id = p.player_id
  WHERE p.birth_country IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
t AS (
  SELECT SUM(cnt) * 1.0 AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(c.cnt) AS sum_counts,
       AVG(c.cnt / t.total) AS avg_share,
       AVG(c.cnt - t.avg_cnt) AS avg_diff
FROM c, t
WHERE c.cnt > t.avg_cnt;
